summary: The boundary probe resolved both comparisons, so I recorded the observation and judged it without overstating. Control: the leader's real heartbeat set follower 2's reported leader to 1 (index 56 of CheckRun 2bb2e787750a4a799620f0b0d1673692). Boundary: the same message type from node 3 with no term field at all was accepted with no error and moved the reported leader to 3 (index 57), contradicting the predicate that a message carrying no term must not change the leader context. Short of asserting a defect, I set the defect claim to unresolved and said why: the module's convention is that a term of zero means a local message and it documents no duty to validate that field for network types, so a defect claim would import a duty the snapshot does not state; what would settle it either way is a source statement assigning that validation to the module or a documented caller duty never to deliver term-less messages. The contrast for the main finding is settled either way: the classification gap is not the only way a peer reaches the lead-setting branch, which is why the finding is framed as a classification omission needing no illegal field, while the illegal-term path requires a byzantine or buggy sender and self-heals in the log on the next genuine leader message. Recorded as a Fact with its receipt plus the child interpretation; remaining limits include that the proposal-misdirection consequence is argued from the branch rather than observed. Validation passed with no execution requested.
